title: Production Reliability and Availability
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and key terms of production reliability and availability.
Choose and interpret a suitable Docker example connected to production reliability and availability.
Predict an expected result and verify it using observable evidence in a controlled environment.

content.intro: This lesson covers Production Reliability and Availability. You will connect the named subtopics from the supplied Docker curriculum to a small, observable example. Work through the visual first, then use the example to form a prediction and check it against the actual behavior.
content.why_it_matters: Production delivery includes more than starting a container: define environment configuration, secret access, storage lifecycle, network exposure, logs/health signals, restart and update behavior, backup/restore, and a documented rollback. Compose is suitable for structured single-host deployments; it is not equivalent to cluster orchestration. Learning production reliability and availability helps you make deployment behavior explicit and repeatable instead of relying on a command that happened to work on one machine.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming that a successful start means the application is ready.
common_mistakes.why: A container can start while its dependent service is unavailable or the application is failing after startup.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect health/status and logs; add a meaningful health check or retry strategy where appropriate.

common_mistakes.problem: Keeping required data only in the container writable layer.
common_mistakes.why: Replacing the container can discard that layer and its application state.
common_mistakes.fix: Select a named volume or an external storage system, then rehearse a restore.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a command without checking context, target, or permissions.
common_mistakes.why: Docker commands affect the active endpoint and can change host resources or publish services.
common_mistakes.fix: Check `docker context show`, use an isolated lab, make the smallest change, and verify the resulting state.
